sanity_expectations: At t=0, dI/dt should be positive for the chosen parameters, so I initially rises from 0.01.
B should lag I: during ascent B<I for a period, while after the infectious peak B should remain elevated above I for a period.

Because infectious_saturation=0.08 is comparable to moderate prevalence, the transmission contribution should become visibly sublinear in I once I approaches order 10^-2 to 10^-1 rather than staying exactly first-order.

As B grows to values comparable to removal_burden_saturation=0.08, both removal amplification and transmission suppression should strengthen, contributing to an earlier/lower peak than a low-B phase would suggest.
S should decrease monotonically because its RHS is nonpositive for nonnegative states.
With the chosen rates over t in [0,25], the trajectory should show rise then decline of I rather than only near-exponential growth or an almost flat signal.
role_corrections: dI_dt: claimed-output/target derivative -> derived target of dependent state I within ode_system (confirmed in context of supplied ODE contract)
t: claimed-input/time axis -> independent variable/time axis (confirmed)
S: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state in ode_system (confirmed)
I: claimed-dynamic state -> dependent variable/target state in ode_system (confirmed/refined from generic dynamic state)
B: claimed-dynamic state -> dynamic state in ode_system (confirmed)
rationale: The supplied typed ODE contract is preserved exactly, so this record is treated as an ode_system with time as the only sampled axis and S, I, B as jointly integrated states. Chosen parameters keep all denominators positive and place the dynamics away from parent-recovery limits: transmission_burden_gain=1 and removal_burden_gain=1.2 make burden B materially affect both transmission suppression and removal escalation once B rises; burden_adjustment_rate=1 gives a visible but not extreme lag so B tracks I with phase delay rather than collapsing immediately to I; infectious_saturation=0.08 is comparable to moderate infectious fractions, so source-side transmission becomes sublinear once I leaves the seed regime, but not so small that transmission is quenched from the start. susceptible_saturation=0.25 keeps susceptible limitation active over the reachable S range instead of making transmission nearly linear in S everywhere. transmission_rate=2.2 and removal_rate=0.5 yield initial growth from the inherited initial condition while still allowing decline after susceptible depletion and burden-responsive suppression/removal intensify. The time window [0,25] with 300 points should capture rise, peak, and decline in a closed-population outbreak without requiring altered initial conditions. The intended distinguishing conditions are therefore reached along one trajectory: early low-B behavior is closer to the parent, mid-epidemic elevated B flattens the S-to-incidence relation and boosts removal, and moderate I triggers the added I/(infectious_saturation+I) transmission curvature. Weak effect honesty: very early times remain approximately parent-like because B is initially small and I<<infectious_saturation; the new mechanisms strengthen only after the trajectory enters moderate-I and moderate-B regimes.

scenario_text: Model the rise and decline of an infectious population in a closed population where susceptible depletion is the main source of feedback. Susceptible and infectious fractions are jointly evolved from initial conditions, with infection generated by infectious contacts and infectious individuals removed at a constant rate. Recovered or otherwise removed individuals are not required as a dynamic state because they do not return to susceptibility in the baseline model. The target is the time derivative of the infectious fraction.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed transmission_rate, the target mapping is dI_dt = I*(transmission_rate*S - removal_rate), so for fixed I the dependence on S is linear with constant slope transmission_rate*I and a single threshold at S = removal_rate/transmission_rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the constant transmission effectiveness by a susceptibility-limited contact function so that dI_dt remains proportional to I but its dependence on S bends away from strict linearity; the marginal effect of additional susceptible fraction changes with S instead of staying constant.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that visit both low-S and high-S regimes, infectious growth accelerates less-than-linearly at low susceptible availability and approaches the parent law only in the weak-saturation limit, changing early decline/growth curvature and shifting the approach to the infection peak.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories span a nontrivial range of susceptible fraction, especially when S is not uniformly near zero and not confined to an infinitesimal neighborhood where any smooth refinement is locally linear; the contrast is strongest when depletion carries S from high to moderate/low values during the observed window.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as altered curvature of dI_dt versus S along epidemic rise and decline under the same initial-condition protocol. In holdout trajectories that deplete susceptibility further, the same saturation of transmission effectiveness produces a larger deviation from the parent's linear-in-S mapping.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the susceptibility-saturation correction becomes negligible over the observed S range, yielding an effectively constant transmission gain.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes each added susceptible individual contributes the same incremental transmission opportunity regardless of susceptible availability, i.e. strictly mass-action incidence with no saturation or diminishing returns in effective contact formation.
plan.baseline_assumption: Transmission characteristics are constant through time and enter infection generation as an exactly bilinear homogeneous-mixing term transmission_rate*S*I.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Saturating effective contact formation or partial contact limitation, where the conversion of available susceptibles into realized infectious contacts has diminishing returns as susceptible availability changes, while removal remains first-order.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the exact bilinear incidence assumption rather than adding a wholly new compartment. The parent target mapping uses a single gain on S: for fixed I, increasing S changes dI_dt with constant slope. A child with susceptibility-limited transmission changes the mapping itself, not just an auxiliary trajectory, because dI_dt as a function of observed S and I is no longer linear in S. The distinguishing condition is to compare portions of observed trajectories with the same order of magnitude of I but different susceptible availability: hold removal_rate fixed and use the standard initial conditions so that S declines over time. Under the parent, one refitted transmission_rate gives the same marginal sensitivity of dI_dt to S everywhere. Under the child, that sensitivity is stronger in one S regime and weaker in another, producing different curvature and a shifted peak condition along the same observable epidemic course. This is scientifically admissible in closed-population outbreaks where contact realization or susceptible accessibility is not perfectly proportional to S. The limitation is that if observations only cover an extremely narrow S interval, the refinement may be hard to distinguish because any smooth nonlinear incidence looks approximately linear there.

contract.difficulty_rationale: The child nests the observed susceptible state inside a nonlinear availability map before multiplying by I, so the target cannot be matched by only retuning a single global transmission gain. This is structurally harder because the slope of dI_dt with respect to S changes across the same trajectory rather than remaining constant.
contract.assumption_before: Transmission characteristics are constant through time and enter infection generation as an exactly bilinear homogeneous-mixing term transmission_rate*S*I.
contract.assumption_after: Realized infectious contacts are limited by susceptible accessibility, so transmission uses a saturating function of susceptible availability rather than exact bilinear mass action.
contract.parent_reduction: When susceptible_saturation is small relative to the observed S range, S/(susceptible_saturation + S) is close to 1 and the child approaches transmission_rate*I - removal_rate*I over that range; more generally the child behaves like an effectively constant transmission gain only if the observed S interval is narrow enough that the nonlinear factor is nearly constant.
contract.observable_signature: For fixed or similar I values sampled along trajectories, the parent predicts dI_dt changes linearly with S with constant slope, whereas the child predicts a concave dependence on S through transmission_rate*S/(susceptible_saturation + S). The difference is observable when epidemic trajectories traverse both higher and lower susceptible fractions under the same initial-condition protocol, producing changed curvature in growth-to-decline transition and a shifted infectious peak condition.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent transmission_rate cannot reproduce both the higher effective sensitivity in one susceptible regime and the weaker sensitivity in another because the parent enforces constant slope with respect to S for fixed I. Matching one part of the trajectory forces systematic error in another whenever the observed S range is broad enough for the saturation factor to vary appreciably.

response_change.parent_relation: The per-infectious growth term is proportional to I with a susceptibility-dependent coefficient transmission_rate*S/(susceptible_saturation + S), so dI_dt changes linearly with I at fixed S.
response_change.child_relation: Retain susceptibility-limited transmission but relax the assumption of first-order removal by allowing removal pressure to increase with infectious burden, so dI_dt acquires additional downward curvature as I grows even at the same S.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar S but different I during the ascent, the child predicts stronger suppression of growth at larger I and an earlier, flatter peak; the parent keeps the same linear-in-I growth-minus-removal shape and cannot match both low-I near-exponential rise and high-I self-limited slowdown with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when infectious prevalence is not negligible, so that burden-dependent removal or isolation saturation effects become comparable to baseline first-order removal; practically, intermediate-to-high I relative to the initial seed while S is still appreciable.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: The same outbreak trajectory contains low-I and higher-I phases: near introduction the child reduces to the parent-like linear law, while later on the same run the added infectious-burden dependence bends the I-growth curve downward more strongly, extending naturally into holdout segments with larger peaks.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing burden dependence in removal, the child recovers the parent law exactly.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes infectious removal is strictly first-order and independent of current prevalence, omitting realistic prevalence-dependent clearance or isolation responses that intensify as case burden rises.
plan.baseline_assumption: Removal characteristics are constant through time and proportional only to the current infectious fraction with coefficient removal_rate.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Burden-dependent removal/isolation: as more individuals are infectious, detection, self-isolation, or control actions increase effective exit from the infectious pool, producing nonlinear prevalence-dependent removal.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the idealized first-order removal law rather than add an unrelated process. The parent target mapping is single-phase: for any fixed S, dI_dt is linear in I with one net coefficient. Vary I along the observed outbreak trajectory while holding the susceptibility level approximately matched across nearby times or across runs with the same initial conditions and parameter settings. Under admissible conditions where I grows beyond the tiny-seed regime but S has not yet collapsed, the child predicts extra negative curvature in dI_dt versus I, causing slower growth at larger prevalence and a broader, earlier peak. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot create that curvature because changing removal_rate or transmission_rate only shifts the linear coefficient uniformly across all I. This change affects the scored target mapping directly, not only an auxiliary state, and remains scientifically consistent with a closed population and nonnegative bounded fractions.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when infectious burden changes on a timescale comparable to or faster than behavioral, detection, or isolation adjustment, especially during epidemic ascent and shortly after the peak when I is moderate and changing appreciably.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, delayed removal appears as steeper ascent or postponed downturn relative to the same contemporaneous S and I levels; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to stronger hysteresis-like differences between rising and falling phases at matched prevalence.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the adjustment timescale to zero so the burden-response state tracks I quasi-instantaneously, collapsing delayed removal back to the instantaneous function of I.
plan.promotion_reason: A delay in burden-dependent removal cannot be represented by refitting only the existing instantaneous S- and I-dependent mapping; one memory state is needed to encode recent infectious burden under the ODE contract.
plan.gap_statement: The model assumes that burden-triggered removal or isolation reacts immediately to current prevalence, omitting realistic response delays from symptom recognition, testing, tracing, and behavior change.
plan.baseline_assumption: Transmission and removal characteristics are constant through time.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Delayed activation of burden-dependent removal/isolation through a finite-response control or detection process tracking recent infectious burden.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's instantaneous-response assumption for the already present burden-dependent removal mechanism. Vary time along observed trajectories while holding the model parameters and initial conditions fixed. In the parent, once current S and I are specified, dI_dt is fully determined: there is a single-phase mapping with no dependence on whether the epidemic is rising or falling. In the child, delayed adjustment of removal pressure means that two times with similar current S and I can have different dI_dt if one occurs on the way up, before control has caught up, and the other on the way down, after elevated control persists. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not just an auxiliary trajectory, because dI_dt at the same current observed state becomes history-sensitive through one added state. The contrast is admissible in the given closed-population epidemic setting when prevalence changes fast enough that response lags matter; if adjustment is effectively instantaneous, the added mechanism collapses back to the parent and may be hard to identify.

response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar current S and I but different recent growth histories, the child permits different dI_dt values because control/removal pressure lags; the parent gives the same dI_dt whenever current S and I match.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when B becomes appreciable before S is nearly depleted, so recent burden is high enough to alter contact success or precautionary behavior while transmission is still active; weak when B≈0 or late when S is already very small.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early epidemic data with low B remain close to the parent law, while later intervals with elevated B show extra attenuation of infection generation at similar S; in holdout, trajectories with faster burden build-up amplify this same state-dependent suppression.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added burden effect on transmission to zero, equivalently making effective susceptible saturation independent of B.
plan.gap_statement: The model allows burden-responsive control only through faster removal, but assumes transmission opportunities respond to susceptible availability with one fixed saturation scale regardless of recent epidemic burden.
plan.baseline_assumption: The half-saturation governing effective contact formation is constant and unaffected by perceived or acted-on burden.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Recent burden can trigger voluntary distancing, reduced contact intensity, or operational congestion that lowers realized transmission per susceptible contact, even before removal occurs; this acts as burden-dependent suppression of transmission efficiency.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase transmission assumption rather than add an unrelated compartment. The parent target mapping from observed states to dI_dt is separable in the transmission part: for fixed I and parameters, the infection-generation term is only a function of S, while B influences only removal. Varying condition: compare times or trajectories with similar S and I but different lagged burden B generated by different epidemic histories under the same initial-condition contract. Held fixed: transmission_rate, removal_rate, and the supplied states S and I at the comparison point. Parent contrast: once S and I are fixed, changing B can only steepen the removal term linearly through its own saturating branch; it cannot also flatten the susceptible-to-incidence relationship. This is scientifically admissible in closed-population epidemics with behavior or contact adaptation tied to recent burden. plan.activation_condition: Observable when I reaches a non-negligible fraction of the population while S remains above the contact-limitation scale, so repeated contacts, local overlap, or finite effective mixing make added infectious individuals less than proportionally productive; weak when I stays very small throughout.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early-to-mid epidemic growth already shows slight downward bending of dI_dt versus I at moderate prevalence; in holdout, larger peaks extend this same mechanism into clearer sublinear transmission and stronger peak flattening without changing the sign structure.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the infectious-saturation scale to infinity, which restores exactly first-order transmission in I.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes every additional infectious individual contributes proportionally to new infections at all prevalence levels, after only susceptible-side and burden-side suppression are applied.
plan.baseline_assumption: Transmission is first-order in the infectious fraction, with no saturation or overlap on the infectious source side.
plan.scientific_mechanism: At moderate prevalence, infectious individuals increasingly compete for the same susceptible contacts or share overlapping contact neighborhoods, so total force of infection rises sublinearly with infectious abundance even in a closed homogeneous benchmark.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent’s exact mass-action dependence on I within the transmission term, not to add a wholly new biological process. The parent already includes susceptible limitation and burden-responsive suppression, but it still uses a single-phase linear infectiousness law: holding S, B, and parameters fixed, the transmission part of dI_dt scales exactly with I. Varying prevalence over trajectories while keeping the same parameter set and the same initial-condition contract, this implies one shared local slope of transmission with respect to I near low and moderate prevalence. In the child, the slope decreases as I grows because infectious contribution saturates, creating changed curvature in the scored target mapping dI_dt(S,I,B). This contrast is scientifically admissible when prevalence becomes moderate before susceptibles are exhausted; then overlap in contacted susceptibles or finite effective mixing reduces marginal transmission per extra infectious individual. The effect is not merely in an auxiliary state because it directly changes the target equation’s dependence on observed I. Limitation: if all observed trajectories remain in the very low-I regime, the refinement is weakly identifiable and the parent is approximately recovered.

contract.activation_condition: Observable when I reaches a non-negligible fraction of the population while S remains above the contact-limitation scale, so repeated contacts, local overlap, or finite effective mixing make added infectious individuals less than proportionally productive; weak when I stays very small throughout.
contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early-to-mid epidemic growth already shows slight downward bending of dI_dt versus I at moderate prevalence; in holdout, larger peaks extend this same mechanism into clearer sublinear transmission and stronger peak flattening without changing the sign structure.
contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the infectious-saturation scale to infinity, which restores exactly first-order transmission in I.
contract.domain_mechanism: source-side saturation of infectious contribution to transmission
contract.scientific_mechanism: At moderate prevalence, infectious individuals increasingly compete for the same susceptible contacts or share overlapping contact neighborhoods, so total force of infection rises sublinearly with infectious abundance even in a closed homogeneous benchmark.
contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the target mapping with respect to I: the marginal transmission slope decreases with I, creating curvature that cannot be matched by simply rescaling transmission_rate or other existing parent parameters.
contract.assumption_before: Transmission is first-order in the infectious fraction, with no saturation or overlap on the infectious source side.
contract.assumption_after: Transmission from infectious individuals has finite effective capacity, so source-side contribution saturates with I.
contract.parent_reduction: Taking infectious_saturation to infinity recovers the parent transmission law.
contract.observable_signature: At fixed S and B, the child predicts a concave-down transmission contribution as I increases, so trajectories that enter moderate-I regimes while S is still substantial show earlier slowdown and lower, broader peaks than the parent. range_suggestions.infectious_saturation: positive; typically comparable to moderate infectious fractions where source-side overlap begins to reduce marginal transmission, e.g. from well below 1 up to several times the observed I range

domain_mechanisms.description: contact or transmission response changes with prevalence or density
risk response changes contact or control behavior
finite immunity duration or recovery transition

baseline_mechanisms: Transmission from infectious to susceptible individuals.
Removal of infectious individuals through recovery, isolation, or disease-related exit.
Feedback from declining susceptibility to the rate of new infection.
baseline_assumptions: The population is closed over the modeled interval.
Mixing is homogeneous, with no age, spatial, or network structure.
Transmission and removal characteristics are constant through time.
Removed individuals do not return to the susceptible class.
scientific_constraints: S and I must remain nonnegative.
The susceptible and infectious fractions must remain bounded by the population total.
The susceptible fraction cannot increase in the baseline model.
The infectious fraction cannot exceed the available population fraction.
refinement_agenda: Add loss of immunity or reinfection.
Introduce time-varying control, behavior, or transmission conditions.
Split the population into age groups, locations, or risk classes.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed transmission_rate, the target mapping is dI_dt = I*(transmission_rate*S - removal_rate), so for fixed I the dependence on S is linear with constant slope transmission_rate*I and a single threshold at S = removal_rate/transmission_rate.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the constant transmission effectiveness by a susceptibility-limited contact function so that dI_dt remains proportional to I but its dependence on S bends away from strict linearity; the marginal effect of additional susceptible fraction changes with S instead of staying constant.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that visit both low-S and high-S regimes, infectious growth accelerates less-than-linearly at low susceptible availability and approaches the parent law only in the weak-saturation limit, changing early decline/growth curvature and shifting the approach to the infection peak.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories span a nontrivial range of susceptible fraction, especially when S is not uniformly near zero and not confined to an infinitesimal neighborhood where any smooth refinement is locally linear; the contrast is strongest when depletion carries S from high to moderate/low values during the observed window.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as altered curvature of dI_dt versus S along epidemic rise and decline under the same initial-condition protocol. In holdout trajectories that deplete susceptibility further, the same saturation of transmission effectiveness produces a larger deviation from the parent's linear-in-S mapping.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the susceptibility-saturation correction becomes negligible over the observed S range, yielding an effectively constant transmission gain.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Saturating effective contact formation or partial contact limitation, where the conversion of available susceptibles into realized infectious contacts has diminishing returns as susceptible availability changes, while removal remains first-order.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: The child nests the observed susceptible state inside a nonlinear availability map before multiplying by I, so the target cannot be matched by only retuning a single global transmission gain. This is structurally harder because the slope of dI_dt with respect to S changes across the same trajectory rather than remaining constant.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Transmission characteristics are constant through time and enter infection generation as an exactly bilinear homogeneous-mixing term transmission_rate*S*I.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Realized infectious contacts are limited by susceptible accessibility, so transmission uses a saturating function of susceptible availability rather than exact bilinear mass action.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: When susceptible_saturation is small relative to the observed S range, S/(susceptible_saturation + S) is close to 1 and the child approaches transmission_rate*I - removal_rate*I over that range; more generally the child behaves like an effectively constant transmission gain only if the observed S interval is narrow enough that the nonlinear factor is nearly constant.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: For fixed or similar I values sampled along trajectories, the parent predicts dI_dt changes linearly with S with constant slope, whereas the child predicts a concave dependence on S through transmission_rate*S/(susceptible_saturation + S). The difference is observable when epidemic trajectories traverse both higher and lower susceptible fractions under the same initial-condition protocol, producing changed curvature in growth-to-decline transition and a shifted infectious peak condition.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent transmission_rate cannot reproduce both the higher effective sensitivity in one susceptible regime and the weaker sensitivity in another because the parent enforces constant slope with respect to S for fixed I. Matching one part of the trajectory forces systematic error in another whenever the observed S range is broad enough for the saturation factor to vary appreciably.

response_change.parent_relation: The per-infectious growth term is proportional to I with a susceptibility-dependent coefficient transmission_rate*S/(susceptible_saturation + S), so dI_dt changes linearly with I at fixed S.
response_change.child_relation: Retain susceptibility-limited transmission but relax the assumption of first-order removal by allowing removal pressure to increase with infectious burden, so dI_dt acquires additional downward curvature as I grows even at the same S.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar S but different I during the ascent, the child predicts stronger suppression of growth at larger I and an earlier, flatter peak; the parent keeps the same linear-in-I growth-minus-removal shape and cannot match both low-I near-exponential rise and high-I self-limited slowdown with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when infectious prevalence is not negligible, so that burden-dependent removal or isolation saturation effects become comparable to baseline first-order removal; practically, intermediate-to-high I relative to the initial seed while S is still appreciable.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: The same outbreak trajectory contains low-I and higher-I phases: near introduction the child reduces to the parent-like linear law, while later on the same run the added infectious-burden dependence bends the I-growth curve downward more strongly, extending naturally into holdout segments with larger peaks.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: In the limit of vanishing burden dependence in removal, the child recovers the parent law exactly.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Burden-dependent removal/isolation: as more individuals are infectious, detection, self-isolation, or control actions increase effective exit from the infectious pool, producing nonlinear prevalence-dependent removal.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it preserves the low-I parent slope while changing the high-I response through a saturating nonlinear modulation of removal, creating state-dependent curvature that cannot be reproduced by globally retuning transmission_rate or removal_rate.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Removal characteristics are constant through time and proportional only to the current infectious fraction with coefficient removal_rate.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Removal increases with infectious burden through a finite-capacity saturating activation of the effective per-capita removal rate.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: At matched or nearly matched susceptible levels, dI_dt versus I is linear in the parent but bends downward in the child once I becomes comparable to removal_burden_saturation; the child therefore shows parent-like early growth from the seed yet stronger slowdown and a broader, earlier peak at moderate-to-high prevalence.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set only changes the constant net linear coefficient multiplying I at fixed S. It cannot simultaneously preserve the small-I ascent and add stronger suppression only at larger I, because any adjustment to removal_rate or transmission_rate affects all prevalence levels uniformly rather than introducing the required I-dependent curvature.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed S, the parent maps I to dI_dt with transmission proportional to I and burden-dependent removal responding instantaneously to the current infectious fraction.
response_change.child_relation: At fixed S and current I, dI_dt depends on a lagged control burden state driven by recent infection levels, so removal escalation is delayed relative to growth.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories with similar current S and I but different recent growth histories, the child permits different dI_dt values because control/removal pressure lags; the parent gives the same dI_dt whenever current S and I match.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when infectious burden changes on a timescale comparable to or faster than behavioral, detection, or isolation adjustment, especially during epidemic ascent and shortly after the peak when I is moderate and changing appreciably.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, delayed removal appears as steeper ascent or postponed downturn relative to the same contemporaneous S and I levels; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to stronger hysteresis-like differences between rising and falling phases at matched prevalence.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the adjustment timescale to zero so the burden-response state tracks I quasi-instantaneously, collapsing delayed removal back to the instantaneous function of I.
evolution_contracts.promotion_reason: A delay in burden-dependent removal cannot be represented by refitting only the existing instantaneous S- and I-dependent mapping; one memory state is needed to encode recent infectious burden under the ODE contract.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: Finite-time adjustment of removal pressure to recent infectious burden
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Delayed activation of burden-dependent removal/isolation through a finite-response control or detection process tracking recent infectious burden.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: The child first combines current and past burden through a dynamical tracking state and then applies the existing saturating nonlinear removal activation to that lagged state. This adds true memory and phase dependence to the target mapping, which cannot be reproduced by a coefficient-only correction of an instantaneous prevalence law.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Burden-triggered removal or isolation responds instantaneously to the current infectious fraction.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Burden-triggered removal or isolation responds to a finite-response burden state that relaxes toward the current infectious fraction.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: As burden_adjustment_rate becomes large, B approaches I along trajectories and the target law recovers the parent expression.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: At matched observed S and I along one trajectory, rising-phase points can have larger dI_dt than falling-phase points because B lags below I during ascent and remains above I during decline; this changes the scored dI_dt mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary state. The effect is visible when burden_adjustment_rate is not much larger than epidemic growth or decay rates and I traverses values comparable to removal_burden_saturation so the nonlinear activation is appreciable.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set defines one instantaneous mapping from current S and I to dI_dt, so it cannot assign different derivatives to the same contemporaneous S and I reached with different recent histories. Refitting transmission_rate, removal_rate, removal_burden_gain, susceptible_saturation, or removal_burden_saturation only rescales or reshapes that single-valued surface; it does not create the required history-dependent phase split across admissible trajectories.

response_change.parent_relation: Net infectious growth depends on current susceptible availability through a single saturating transmission factor transmission_rate*S/(susceptible_saturation + S), so the per-capita infection term is always approximately linear in S at low S and approaches one fixed saturation scale.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the fixed susceptible half-saturation by a burden-responsive effective saturation so transmission is further suppressed when recent burden B is high, making susceptibility-to-incidence coupling depend jointly on S and B rather than on S alone.
response_change.observable_effect: At the same S, higher recent burden produces lower infection generation than the parent allows, with the strongest contrast during mid-epidemic periods when B has risen but susceptibles are not yet exhausted; this changes the curvature and peak timing of dI_dt versus S along observed trajectories.

diagnostic_groups.name: burden_activation

diagnostic_groups.name: joint_mid_epidemic_regime

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when B becomes appreciable before S is nearly depleted, so recent burden is high enough to alter contact success or precautionary behavior while transmission is still active; weak when B≈0 or late when S is already very small.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, early epidemic data with low B remain close to the parent law, while later intervals with elevated B show extra attenuation of infection generation at similar S; in holdout, trajectories with faster burden build-up amplify this same state-dependent suppression.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added burden effect on transmission to zero, equivalently making effective susceptible saturation independent of B.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: burden-responsive suppression of transmission efficiency through a state-dependent saturation scale
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Recent burden can trigger voluntary distancing, reduced contact intensity, or operational congestion that lowers realized transmission per susceptible contact, even before removal occurs; this acts as burden-dependent suppression of transmission efficiency.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because B now changes the shape of the susceptibility-to-transmission response, not just its overall gain, so the local slope with respect to S varies across burden levels.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The half-saturation governing effective contact formation is constant and unaffected by perceived or acted-on burden.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: The effective susceptible half-saturation increases with recent burden, so burden suppresses transmission by flattening the susceptible-response curve.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: Setting transmission_burden_gain = 0 recovers the parent exactly.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: Comparing observed times or trajectories with similar S and I but different B, the child predicts lower dI_dt at higher B not only through stronger removal but also through a flatter transmission response in S; this is most visible in mid-epidemic regimes with appreciable B and still-moderate S, where peaks occur earlier or lower than the parent permits with one shared parameter set.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both low-B and high-B phases when the slope of the transmission contribution with respect to S changes with B, because in the parent B affects only the removal branch and leaves the S-to-transmission curvature fixed. Retuning transmission_rate or susceptible_saturation can shift one common transmission curve, but cannot make that curve flatten selectively at high burden while remaining unchanged at low burden across the same observed state space.
